title: Series Basics: One Path, One Current
description: Three resistors in a single loop across a 12 V source. Find the total resistance, the one circuit current, the drop across each resistor and the total power, then confirm that the drops add up to the source (KVL).

tasks.question: What is the total resistance of the circuit?
What current does the 12 V source deliver?
What is the voltage across R2 (200 Ω)?
What is the voltage across R3 (300 Ω)?
What is the current through R1? (Think before you calculate.)
What total power does the source supply?

hints: Series resistances add: R_total = R1 + R2 + R3.
There is only one path, so the current through every resistor equals the source current, I = V_source ÷ R_total.
Each drop is I × R for that resistor. The largest resistor drops the most voltage. The three drops must add to 12 V.
Total power is V_source × I_total. You can also add the three I² × R values and get the same number.
learningGoals: Apply the series resistance rule and Ohm's law together.
Recognize that current is identical in every element of a series circuit.
Verify a solution with Kirchhoff's voltage law.
disclaimer: Simulated bench exercise; not field experience.
